new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (21 pp., extracted from the open DLI/archive.org scan of BSOS vol. 5, item;ernet.dli.2015.70629). I rendered p.1 (= journal p.323) to an image and read it: the third paragraph, immediately before the 'Alphabet' heading, reads exactly 'The accent in Lau, where noticeable, is on the first syllable, and the voice is raised at the end of the sentence with a stressing of the penultimate syllable.' The text ( lines 19-21) matches. a full-text search for stress/accent the whole article for accent/stress/penult/emphasis finds no other prosodic remark (the other 'emphasis' hits are about emphatic pronouns/particles). Surrounding section: p.323 intro locates the language on the artificial island…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent, to the extent it is perceptible at all, falls on the first syllable of the word; separately, at the end of a sentence the pitch rises and the penultimate syllable (of the sentence-final word) is stressed, i.e. a phrase-final penultimate prominence overlaid on weak word-initial accent.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the hedge 'where noticeable' signals that word accent is weak. No statement about long vowels attracting accent, though vowel length is described as distinctive (long vowels written double).
new_statements.domain_note: Two domains are distinguished in the one sentence: word-level accent (initial) versus sentence-final prosody (raised voice plus penultimate stress). Impressionistic missionary-era description based on five months at Fouia/Sulufou (Lau Lagoon, 'Lau proper') in 1927; no instrumental or metrical analysis. Consistent in direction with the left-edge (initial) stress described for the closely related North Malaitan language Toqabaqita in our catalog, but that is a different language and was not used as evidence here.
new_statements.identity_note: Ivens 1929 explicitly describes 'Lau proper' as spoken on Sulufou (Sulu Vou) and the other artificial islands of the Lau Lagoon, north-east coast of Malaita (fieldwork at Fouia, 1927) = Glottolog lauu1247. His earlier 1921 grammar (no stress statement) was based on the southern Lau of Port Adam (Ataa Cove emigrants), which he says is closer to the hill languages. Tryon 1995 distinguishes three Lau dialects (Suafa, Lau, Dai/Ndai); the statement pertains to the central Lau dialect.

new_statements.relation_note: Near-verbatim restatement by the same author of the Ivens 1929 BSOS grammar sentence already in existing_statements ('accent.. on the first syllable.. voice raised at the end of the sentence with a stressing of the penultimate syllable'); same placement as the catalog record (initial). Adds only the explicit dialect basis (Sulu Fou, NE Malaita lagoon) and drops the 1929 hedge 'where noticeable'. Instalments 2, 4 and 7 (pp. 21-130) were also downloaded and searched: vocabulary and English index only, no further accent/stress remarks. new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent is on the first syllable of the word; in addition, at the end of a sentence the voice is raised and the penultimate syllable (of the sentence-final stretch) receives accentuation, i.e. a sentence-level final-penult prominence on top of word-initial accent.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing on secondary stress. The only additional prosodic remark is sentence-level: raised voice at sentence end with accentuation of the penultimate syllable.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for word accent (unlike the 1929 grammar's hedge 'where noticeable', the 1932 note states the rule flatly). Other notes concern the glottal 'break' (dropped consonants g, k, l, n, s, t), explosive onset of 'a after a break, vowel length by doubling, and the a/e Umlaut.
new_statements.identity_note: Ivens 1932, Note 7 (p. 3): 'The basis of this vocabulary is the speech of the people of Sulu Fou, one of the artificial islands in the lagoon on the northeast coast of Big Mala' -- i.e. the Lau lagoon variety of North-East Malaita (Sulufou), the same variety as his 1921 and 1929 grammars; this is Lau of Malaita (lauu1247), not the Lau Islands of Fiji.
